fama_french_3_factor_model.text:
`fama_french_5_factor_model` extends `fama_french_3_factor_model` by adding two factors: profitability (RMW) and investment (CMA). The 3-factor version regresses portfolio excess returns on market, size (SMB) and value (HML) factors, so it answers: how much of the portfolio's return is explained by market, size and value exposure, and what alpha is left? The 5-factor version asks the same question with profitability and investment exposure also accounted for, so its alpha is measured after those two effects as well.

In practice, the difference is the `factors` input. The 3-factor function takes a matrix with 3 columns (MKT, SMB, HML), while `fama_french_5_factor_model` takes 5 columns (MKT, SMB, HML, RMW, CMA). Both take the same `excess_returns` input and both estimate coefficients with the same regression formula.

explain.text: `fama_french_5_factor_model` runs a Fama-French 5-factor regression of a portfolio's excess returns (returns over the risk-free rate) on five factor return series: market (MKT), size (SMB), value (HML), profitability (RMW) and investment (CMA). It extends the 3-factor model by adding the profitability and investment factors. The regression has an intercept (alpha) plus a beta for each factor, estimated by ordinary least squares. You supply `excess_returns` and `factors`, an (n_obs, 5) matrix with one column per factor. pyvar does the calculation, so the output is the fitted alpha and factor loadings for your data.

when.text:
The Fama French 5 Factor Model (`fama_french_5_factor_model`) fits when you want to explain a portfolio's returns using five common risk factors.

- You have a series of portfolio excess returns over the risk-free rate (`excess_returns`) and matching factor returns for MKT, SMB, HML, RMW and CMA (`factors`).
- You want to see how much of the portfolio's return loads on profitability (RMW) and investment (CMA), beyond the market, size and value factors.
- You want a regression-based estimate of alpha and factor betas, fitted by ordinary least squares.
- You're comparing a richer factor description against a simpler one for the same portfolio.

If you only need market, size and value, `fama_french_3_factor_model` is listed as the 3-factor regression (MKT, SMB, HML).
